title: Print Window Chrome Fill Cutouts
description: In the print report, windows are drawn with a top line/row that has small chip elements (tabs) on the left and right ends — e.g. a project/tab chip on the left and a page-number/control chip on the right. The window's border (outline stroke) already renders correctly, tracing the stepped shape: a "U" cutout when both left and right chips are present, and an "L" cutout when only the left chip is present. However, the window's background fill does not follow this same stepped shape — it doesn't have the matching U/L cutouts, so the fill is likely a plain rectangle that either bleeds into the notch area or fails to fill it correctly, creating a visual mismatch against the correctly-drawn border. Need to find where the window chrome fill is painted (likely print/tex/semio-window.sty: the cap/tab/gap painting commands such as semio@window@cap@paint, semio@window@header@gap@paint, semio@window@cap, semio@heading@pair, semio@heading@cap@muted, semio@paragraph@cap@muted, and the tcolorbox colback fill for the body) and correct the fill logic so it matches the border's U/L stepped outline in both the two-chip and one-chip cases.
summary: Corrected the first fix. Root cause of the follow-up regression: `\semio@window@header@close@paint` (added by the first pass) drew a top border line flush with the chip plus a right-edge vertical stroke and canvas fill across the entire remaining row width — this closes the L-shape "properly" in isolation, but visually reads as a second full-width bordered rectangle stacked on top of the actual window body, since every unnumbered header (all `Window`-environment cover rows in mit-bestand's Zwischenbericht front page — "Zukunft Bau", "Titel", "Untertitel", "Antragstellende Institution", etc.) is L-shape by construction (`\semio_window_generic_begin:n` always clears the number). Fixed by removing `\semio@window@header@close@paint` entirely and rewriting `\semio@window@header@gap@paint` (now single-arg) to paint a true transparent cutout: reserves height with an invisible `\rule{0pt}{...}` strut (no fill rectangle) and draws only the baseline hairline stroke — no top border, no right-edge closure. `\semio@window@header@muted` still branches on whether a ctrl/number chip exists, but both branches now call the same fill-less gap paint, so the border hugs only the chip(s) and the rest of the row is a real cutout down to the window's own border, matching the on-screen app's `windowGapFrameClass` (no background class, border-b only). Updated the other 3 call sites (`\semio@heading@pair`, `\semio@heading@pair@muted`, `\semio@heading@pair@muted@num`, `\semio@window@gap@inbox`) to the new single-argument signature. Verified two ways: (1) a from-scratch minimal harness (verify-minimal-muted.tex, stubbing every dependency) compiles cleanly and renders both the L-shape ("Verzeichnis der Abbildungen") and U-shape ("Ein Beispielbild" / "1.a") headers correctly — chip-only border, single connecting baseline, no extra box; (2) rebuilt the real mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht front page end-to-end and confirmed pixel-zoomed that "Zukunft Bau" and the other cover chips now show a tight border around the chip plus one thin line to the margin, not a solid double-bordered block. Note: the shared print/tex/semio-window.sty file was under concurrent, unrelated, in-progress editing by another session throughout this work (an experimental "WindowBreakParts" page-break-continuation feature) — several full-document test builds intermittently failed with unrelated TeX errors from that in-flux code; this was diagnosed via an isolated HEAD+patch copy and does not affect this fix, which was independently verified in a dependency-free harness.
